newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: S.AFRICAN MPS SIDESTEP CONFRONTATION ON TAX UPSET.
newsitem.headline: S.AFRICAN MPS SIDESTEP CONFRONTATION ON TAX UPSET.

text.p: South Africa's parliamentary finance committee on Tuesday backed out of confrontation over the controversial resignation of the country's top tax chief.

Parliamentarians and tax experts were shocked last week to hear that South African Revenue Services (SARS) chief executive Piet Liebenberg had resigned over differences with Finance Minister Trevor Manuel on the extent of the SARS' autonomy.
Observers said Liebenberg had seemed to want full autonomy, almost amounting to privatisation, for the SARS, while Manuel was only considering administrative autonomy.
Opposition parties immediately called for the parliamentary committee to summon both men to explain what had happened.

They were particularly concerned about how this would affect the ongoing restructuring and strengthening of the now combined customs and excise and inland revenue departments, and the urgent need to improve tax collection.

Financial markets were relatively unfazed by the resignation, with some commentators saying this reflected a growing confidence in Manuel and his team after initial jitters when he took office last year as the first African National Congress finance minister.
Mindful of the possible effects of any messy revelations, ANC committee members were clearly uneasy about the prospect of summoning Manuel and Liebenberg to account for themselves at a joint sitting.
"We are not going to be party to a process that militates against the integrity of (Manuel's) office whilst engaging in so-called imprudent transparency," ANC member Mewa Ramgobin said.
"I therefore motivate that the minister not be subjected, nor a senior citizen (Liebenberg), to an interrogation by this committee."

A compromise was eventually hammered out. Manuel would be asked to brief the committee on how the resignation would affect the management and running of SARS and he would probably designate his deputy, Gill Marcus, to brief it.
Marcus has temporarily been relieved of most of her other duties to ensure the smooth running of the SARS following Liebenberg's departure.
The committee has been pressing for the SARS to be given administrative autonomy so that it can recruit staff at market related, rather than civil service, salaries.
